_doc: Graphics tiers of the persistent city (docs/notes/ue-persistent-city.md). Each tier is a set of console variables over the cinematic preset (render_take_cine2h.json): streaming pools, virtual shadow maps, Lumen and ray tracing, view distance, and the city's own ranges (valdrada.BlocksRangeM: full blocks around the lens, beyond them the far city; valdrada.KitFarRangeM: reduced kit instances; valdrada.RTRangeM: blocks in the ray tracing scene). Targets: low 8 GB, medium 12 GB, high 16 GB, cinematic whatever the GPU has. persist_render.py --tier writes a tier into the job; in a game, valdrada.Tier 0-3 applies it. The level's grids load the actors as far as the largest tier reaches; the plugin loads blocks, builds kit and keeps far stand-ins by distance with the tier's valdrada.*RangeM (2026-10-25: the grids' own ranges did not bound the blocks). 'res' is the tier's output resolution (persist_render.py --prepare writes it into the queue). Proven with a real cap (persist_render.py --vram-cap, a ballast process): low in 8 GB, medium in 12, high in 16, mnHhp79 2026-10-25, docs/notes/ue-persistent-city.md. Startup variables (pools, r.Nanite.Streaming.ReservedResources: Nanite's pages and root pages grow in place instead of a copy holding old and new, a 1 GB allocation the 8 GB cap failed) go on the command line as well (persist_render.py --cooked passes every tier variable through -dpcvars).
